conventions.convention: Assume AC and, where stated, its countable-family consequence. The mass satisfies m>0. The Fourier transform uses exp(−ip·x), with inverse normalization (2π)⁻².

The Gaussian measure is on the cylinder σ-algebra of real tempered distributions. Fix a nonnegative smooth compactly supported mollifier of integral one; symmetry of the mollifier is not assumed. Smearings are samplewise Lebesgue integrals against bounded measurable compactly supported complex functions.
Each Wick polynomial uses its own Gaussian variance. Orders n,m start at zero in the finite covariance identity, with c⁰=1 even when c=0.
Continuum Wick limits are L² equivalence classes; the theorem covers integer n≥1 and uses the complex inner product E[conjugate(X)Y].

The interaction polynomial has even degree at least two and positive leading coefficient; coupling is nonnegative. Exponential integrability, insertion limits, infinite-volume limits, clustering and growth bounds are separate obligations, not consequences asserted by the contract.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC and its countable-family consequence, for m>0 the covariance multiplier (|p|²+m²)⁻¹ is represented off zero by G_m(z)=(4π)⁻¹∫₀∞t⁻¹exp(−m²t−|z|²/(4t))dt. The kernel has the stated logarithmic near-zero and exponential large-distance bounds, every finite power q≥1 is locally integrable, and the mixed mollified covariances converge off zero with a uniform logarithmic bound on bounded difference sets.

Assume AC. For centered jointly Gaussian (X,Y), allowing a positive-semidefinite singular covariance matrix, E[:Xⁿ:σ² :Yᵐ:τ²] equals n!cⁿ when n=m and zero otherwise, for all integers n,m≥0, with c⁰:=1.

Under AC and its countable-family consequence, with m>0 and the specified field and fixed mollifier, W_{ε,n}(f) is Cauchy in L²(μ_C) as ε↓0 for every integer n≥1 and bounded measurable compactly supported complex f. Its limit W_n(f) satisfies E[conjugate(W_n(f))W_n(g)]=n!∫∫conjugate(f(x))g(y)G_m(x−y)ⁿ dx dy, and is a real class for real f.

Defines the massive Gaussian field, mollified evaluations Φ_ε(x), variance-normalized finite Wick polynomials through their formal generating series, and samplewise cutoff smearings W_{ε,n}(f). Existence of their L² limits is explicitly deferred to a separate theorem.

concerns.concern: Clause (iii) requires that 'a regulated Schwinger hierarchy' and its limit be constructed, but does not identify its pairings with moments of μ_{Λ_i,λ} or with the normalized insertion limits in clause (ii). The insertion family can also be empty. Thus the written clauses permit an unrelated hierarchy, for example S₀=1 and S_n=0 for n≥1, to satisfy (iii) independently of the specified interaction. State the intended moment identity and the required field-product insertions. The cited source explicitly makes this connection: Summers §3.1, printed p.11, defines the finite-volume Schwinger functions from μ_Λ before taking their volume limit: [Summers](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1203.3991).
